name: Schengen short-stay visa (Category C)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires showing you'll leave the Schengen area at the end of your visit.
This requires showing sufficient funds to cover the visit and return journey.
This requires travel health insurance covering at least €30,000, valid across the Schengen area.
requirements.fix_path: Purchase qualifying Schengen travel health insurance before applying.

evidence_required.document: Travel health insurance certificate (€30,000 minimum coverage)
Evidence of ties to home country and intent to leave

outcome.duration_length: up to 90 days in any 180-day period
outcome.physical_presence_requirement: valid throughout the Schengen area, not just Germany; cannot be used to establish residence

sources.title: Visas for Germany - Federal Foreign Office

notes: Fee €90 confirmed via direct fetch of auswaertiges-amt.de; national (D) visa fee €75 confirmed the same way and reused as the base long-stay visa fee across every other German route in this dataset — worth noting these two figures (€90/€75) as the two most-cited numbers across the entire German dataset. This closes the visit-category gap for Germany, structurally paired with uk_standard_visitor. Unlike the UK's Standard Visitor route, this is a Schengen-wide instrument, not Germany-specific — valid for travel throughout the Schengen area, not just Germany, a genuine structural difference worth surfacing when comparing 'visit' routes across countries (UK, having left the EU, has no Schengen equivalent). Health insurance minimum (€30,000 coverage) is a genuinely distinctive requirement not present on the UK visitor route at all — flagged as a real cross-country difference, not an oversight. Same as uk_standard_visitor: doesn't encode which nationalities are visa-required vs visa-exempt vs need an ETIA S(from 2025-2026, not yet mandatory at verification) — a per-nationality lookup table, not yet built for either country.
